Saved baseline and clarified requirement

rect.data-content:
Trek Learning (Hub/LMS)
Shared dev, staging and production environments.
Recorded as running in the Nov 2 cloud inventory.

TrekCAP / TrekFinder
RD is the identified environment.
An on-demand QA lab workflow is not established.

Scope clarified by the project owner
Add internal QA, sales demo/POC and client pilot environments.
Customer-facing workflows must function end to end.
Pilots must accommodate multiple students.

g.textArea: Proposed: reusable templates, three distinct environment purposes

rect.data-content:
QA, sales or a pilot owner requests an approved environment
Select product, release manifest and purpose-specific profile; assign business and technical owners.
Reuse provisioning code with separate configuration, access, data, capacity and lifecycle policies.

g.textArea: Three purposes, not a fixed instance count; capacity and isolation remain to agree

rect.data-content:
Internal QA
Functional, load and recovery testing.
Repeatable test accounts and data.
May reset or run disruptive experiments.
Isolate impact from customer sessions.

Sales demo / proof of concept
Fully working agreed product workflows.
Ready accounts, data and integrations.
Rehearse before client demonstrations.
Stable sessions; reset on an agreed schedule.

Client pilot
Production-like, working user journeys.
Agreed concurrent students and teachers.
Persistent data, monitoring and support.
Controlled changes and owner-led retirement.

Protect customer use from QA resets, load and fault tests
Separate environment identities, data, deployment targets and state; choose shared infrastructure or dedicated project/cluster by impact.
Identify shared dependencies and validate isolation. A namespace alone may not contain every test or failure.

g.textArea: Expected outcomes
Manifest fields to agree
Controls and lifecycle

rect.data-content:
• QA can reproduce versions and test independently.
• Sales can demonstrate complete, rehearsed workflows.
• Clients can run a supported, multi-student pilot.
• Reuse templates while operating each purpose separately.

• Artifact/template versions, settings and dependencies.
• Data profile, account setup and secret references.
• Purpose, owners, capacity and acceptance criteria.
• Change, retention, reset and retirement policies.

• QA: approved expiry, reset and managed cleanup.
• Demo: stable sessions; controlled data refresh/reset.
• Pilot: retain active data; approved changes and end date.
• Define monitoring, support, recovery and cost owners.

“Fully functioning” needs evidence before customer handoff
All agreed end-to-end workflows, accounts and integrations must pass; pilots must meet agreed concurrent-user and response/error criteria.
Terraform provisions infrastructure; app deployment and acceptance are separate. Use 01B execution controls and approved artifacts from 03/04; production promotion remains a separate decision.

g.textArea: Basis: Nov 12 discussion, Nov 2–3 snapshots and Nov 16 owner clarification. Proposed operating model; agree workload, capacity, owners and service targets before implementation.

g.data-frame: 05B QA, demo and pilot: provision, accept, operate and retire

rect.data-title: 05B QA, demo and pilot: provision, accept, operate and retire

g.textArea: 05B QA, demo and pilot: provision, accept, operate and retire
QA / sales / pilot owner / automation / DevOps | Draft | Provision from code, verify by purpose, accept customer use, then follow the correct lifecycle.
Blue = proposed | Gray = saved evidence or context | Yellow = gate, exception or team decision
QA / sales / pilot request
Provisioning / approvals
Apps / readiness
Acceptance / users / evidence
Lifecycle / DevOps

rect.data-content:
1. Request an environment [Owner]
Choose QA, sales demo/POC or client pilot.
Select manifest, profile, capacity and lifetime.
Name business and technical owners.

Incomplete or unauthorized request
Return findings to the requesting owner.
Correct inputs or obtain required approval.
Do not provision until the request is valid.

Provisioning failed or only partly completed
Hold QA and customer handoff; no assumed rollback.
DevOps reconciles owned resources and state.
Record recovery or cleanup actions.

2. Validate the request [Automation]
Check versions, access, purpose and limits.
Allocate instance ID and ownership scope.
Confirm capacity and required approvals.

3. Review the final target plan
Select purpose-specific inputs and isolated state.
Authorize execution under the agreed policy.
Apply controls: 01B (review or approved policy).

4. Provision infrastructure [Automation]
A scoped executor runs Terraform for this environment.
Verify resources and capture required outputs.
Stop on failed or partial apply.

5. Deploy the selected release [Automation]
Install manifest versions, dependencies and integrations.
Prepare approved accounts, schema and purpose-specific data.
Application deployment is separate from Terraform apply.

6. Check readiness [Automation]
Verify versions, health, access and integrations.
Check accounts, data and monitoring setup.
Send a ready instance for acceptance checks.

Not ready: hold tests and handoff
Return deployment/readiness diagnostics.
Assigned owners correct the setup.
Repeat readiness checks before acceptance.

7. Verify acceptance [QA + owner]
QA: functional, load and recovery checks.
Demo: rehearse agreed end-to-end workflows.
Pilot: verify workflows + concurrent students.
Keep evidence; owner signs off customer use.

8. Use the accepted environment [Owner / users]
QA executes tests; sales demos/POCs; client runs the pilot.
Save versions, outcomes, issues and support history.
Keep customer use stable under agreed change control.

Each purpose follows its own lifecycle
QA: completion/expiry can start approved reset or cleanup. Demo: reset between agreed sessions.
Pilot: keep active data and service; owner approves extension, export/retention and retirement.
No automatic QA cleanup of active customer use. Track costs, residual resources and failure owners.

9. Reset or retire under the agreed policy
Confirm owner approval and data retention/export.
For retirement, stop deployment desired state first.
Clean only owned resources; protect shared services.
Verify residue, cost and evidence/closure records.

g.textArea: Proposed workflow. Agree request interface, approvals, acceptance thresholds, monitoring/support, customer change windows and per-purpose data/lifecycle rules before implementation.

rect.data-content:
Acceptance fails: hold customer handoff
Record failed journeys or capacity checks.
Assign product/environment fixes to owners.
Repeat affected checks and obtain sign-off.

Check infrastructure-code coverage.

rect.data-content:
2. Design reusable environment profiles
Agree manifest, isolation, access and approvals.
Separate QA, demo and pilot configuration/data.
Set capacity, cost and operating policies.
Name business and technical owners.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: DevOps + product + security

rect.data-content:
3. Prove each profile in a trial
Recreate QA; rehearse a full sales demonstration.
Validate a production-like multi-student pilot.
Test integrations, recovery and failure handling.
Capture evidence and owner acceptance.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: QA + sales + pilot owner

rect.data-content:
4. Launch and operate agreed instances
Publish request and acceptance guidance.
Enable monitoring, support and change windows.
Schedule demo resets and pilot data recovery.
Review costs, feedback and owner-led retirement.

g.textArea: Proposed owner: business owner + DevOps
Acceptance evidence before customer use
Dependencies and integration work
Operating controls to agree
Open design decisions

rect.data-content:
• All agreed workflows, accounts and integrations work end to end.
• Pilot meets concurrent-student and response/error thresholds.
• Approved versions, isolation and data persistence are verified.
• Monitoring, support and backup/restore are exercised as agreed.
• QA resets and failed/partial operations cannot disrupt customers.

• Reviewed modules, state scopes and execution identities.
• Release artifacts, deployment path and required integrations.
• Test/demo fixtures; approved pilot data, accounts and secrets.
• Monitoring, support routing, backup/restore and evidence storage.
• Environment ownership, cost visibility and cleanup reconciliation.

• Separate QA disruption from stable demo and pilot use.
• Budget, sizing, quotas and concurrency per environment purpose.
• Approved data handling, access and customer change windows.
• Named support/escalation owner and recovery expectations.
• QA expiry; scheduled demo resets; approved pilot retirement.

• Which workflows, integrations and production similarities are required?
• How many concurrent users; which response/error targets and duration?
• Shared or dedicated resources; which dependencies need isolation?
• Who accepts, supports and authorizes changes for each purpose?
• Which data, backup/restore, retention and end-of-pilot rules apply?

Agree “fully functioning” as measurable acceptance criteria
Every agreed workflow must pass with ready accounts, data and integrations; the pilot must support its agreed multi-student workload and operating requirements.
Use approved 03/04 artifacts and 01 execution controls; coordinate release policy with 11. Production promotion, availability targets and pilot-to-production transition require separate agreement.

g.textArea: Basis: Nov 12 discussion and Nov 16 owner clarification. Three purposes share templates, not QA disruption or automatic cleanup. Counts, capacity, service targets, dates and named owners remain to agree.
